newsitem.title: USA: Dow closes lower as US stock market catches breath.
newsitem.headline: Dow closes lower as US stock market catches breath.

text.p: Wall Street stocks closed slightly lower on Friday, taking a small step back after racing past a series of milestones.

The Dow industrials fell 33 points to close unofficially at 6989, retreating just below the landmark 7000 level in a pre-holiday session dominated by profit-taking. The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 indices also edged lower.
"We saw a little bit of profit-taking today. I don't think there's anything more to read into it," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Over the last three sessions, the Dow had run up by nearly 216 points, driving the S&P 500 index above the 800-point level and the Dow industrials through the 7000 mark.
As if recent economic data hadn't suggested a rosy enough scenario, today's session started with the news that wholesale prices declined in January, the first fall since October 1994.
The news stunned economists and triggered a bond market rally that pushed the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury down to 6.53 percent.

But stocks were unable to follow through on the rally, breathless after their recent run, and with U.S. financial markets closed next Monday for the President's Day holiday, analysts said investors had an added reason to realize some of their most recent-won gains.

"There's a tendency to take profits once the market reaches a plateau and people are thinking 'Let me get this done today so I can have some peace this weekend'," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
With the Dow already at or near many year-end targets set by Wall Street professionals, some strategists predicted prices would soon level off for a time.

"As was the case last year, equity prices have risen substantially during a brief period, about 20 percent since November 1996 and 10 percent since January," Goldman Sachs and Co investment policy committee co-chair Abby Joseph Cohen said today in a research note.

"We believe equity prices could enter a trading range," Cohen said, warning however that, "As was the case in 1996, this would be accompanied by notable volatility and rotation of portfolio holdings."
In individual issues, American Airlines parent company AMR Corp fell 1-1/4 to 81-7/8 as a deadline approached for the company and its pilots' union to reach a labor agreement and avert a strike.
UNC Inc rose 2-1/2 to 13-3/8 after announcing it would merge with Greenwich Air Services Inc in a cash and stock deal worth at least $320 million.
Greenwich Class A shares rose 1-1/8 to 22-3/4.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.34 points to 808.48, snapping at three its series of consecutive record high closes.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.62 points to 1367.19.
